One year after the Gen Z movement, Morocco's youth remain largely absent from parliamentary elections
description: Few Moroccans under 30 – a demographic that has felt ignored by political parties and institutions – are running as candidates. Young Moroccans will likely demonstrate their disillusionment through massive abstention in the September 23 elections.

headline: 'Looksmaxxing' influencer known as 'Clavicular' is charged with rape
description: Braden Peters, the 20-year-old internet personality known for promoting the 'looksmaxxing' trend on social media, has been charged with raping a 17-year-old girl who was heavily intoxicated in May 2025. The lawsuit also accused Peters of injecting the girl with a fat-dissolving substance during a livestream without consent.

headline: UN chief says fossil fuel majors treat atmosphere like 'open sewer'
description: Antonio Guterres slammed the energy industry at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday. 'Those who polluted the most, and profited the most, must do far more to repair the damage they caused,' he urged.

headline: The Catholic Church's new power players: Americans
description: They hold key positions at the Holy See and are establishing think tanks, foundations and universities in Rome. In the wake of their compatriot Robert Prevost, who became Pope Leo XIV in 2025 and whose popularity continues to grow in the United States, American Catholics are throwing their full weight into shaping Catholicism.

Inside the Hamidovic clan's reign of terror over young female pickpockets in the Paris métro
description: They name their children Dior or Al Capone and love designer clothes and luxury cars. To maintain their lavish lifestyle, the men of the Hamidovic clan – a Romani family of Bosnian origin – have maintained a reign of fear over an army of young female pickpockets on Paris public transportation. One branch of the network is on trial in Paris from September 15 to 23.

headline: 'Maoism took root in very diverse places and moments due to its multi-faceted, contradictory and malleable nature'
description: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (7/7). Julia Lovell, a Chinese history and literature professor at Birkbeck, University of London, discusses how Maoism spread. The ideology, she says, benefited from the broader decolonization era, with Mao seen as the foremost anti-imperialist figure.

headline: At Dati's Renault corruption trial, a damning testimony and awkward memos
description: Taking the stand on Monday, MEP Daniel Freund said former French minister Rachida Dati had told the European Parliament she worked as a lawyer on 'domestic violence' cases. She is accused of receiving €900,000 from the Renault-Nissan alliance between 2010 and 2012 in exchange for exerting influence.
